_readme: THE VS CODE MCP CONFIG. VS Code agent mode reads .vscode/mcp.json and
ignores every other host's file, so the se lane needs its own copy.
The extension places it at workspace/.vscode/mcp.json on every
activation, the same declarative way RUNME places the other cages.
IT ATTACHES, IT DOES NOT SPAWN. The extension owns the ONE se server
(HTTP on localhost:7333); agent mode connects to /mcp there. A spawn
here would raise a second engine with a second walk beside the real
one - the exact split the shared server exists to prevent.
THE CAGE DOES NOT COME WITH IT. Claude is caged by a settings file and
the Copilot CLI by --excluded-tools; VS Code agent mode has no
equivalent that a workspace can enforce. Its native tools stay visible.
So on this host contract rule 1 is ADVISORY - the agent is ASKED to
stay in the lane rather than prevented from leaving it.
VERIFY BEFORE TRUSTING IT, the same empirical way copilot-cage.json was
verified: open a session here and ask it to list the exact names of
every tool it can see. Anything that is not an se_ tool is a hole.
